jobs.description:
Job Title: Cloud Delivery Engineer – Infrastructure
Interview Mode: Webcam
Duration: 12+ months
Location: Lansing, MI (Hybrid) (2 days onsite)
 
Engagement:
The State of Michigan is looking for a candidate with a focus on basic cloud engineering Cloud deployment. This role will wear multiple hats assisting State of Michigan Cloud Architects and team to comprehend objectives, generate solutions, POC the solution, generate recommendations then implement the decisions. 
The Entry-Level Cloud Engineer will support the State of Michigan’s cloud architecture and engineering teams in designing, deploying, and maintaining cloud-based solutions across public, private, and hybrid environments. This role is ideal for early‑career technologists who have foundational cloud knowledge and are eager to grow into a full cloud engineering or cloud architecture role.
The engineer will assist senior architects in understanding business objectives, developing solution concepts, performing proof‑of‑concepts, and implementing cloud technologies that improve delivery, automation, and operational efficiency
 




Skill Matrix:


Required

Consultant Expereince

 




Cloud Delivery Analyst / Business Analyst


1-3 years

 

 




Knowledge of concepts of designing and developing dynamic Cloud solutions in Google Cloud Platform and Amazon Web Services and moving parts involved in continuous integration and delivery.


1-3 years

 

 




 




Experience with Tooling and Automation to enable seamless automation of infrastructure provisioning and configuration.


 Highly Desirable

 

 




 




Pipeline Design and Architecture to improve development flow and delivery.


 Highly Desirable

 

 




Solid understanding and skill with DevOps, web services and application programming interfaces (APIs).


 1-3 years

 

 




 




Create, maintain, and troubleshooting skills for cloud infrastructure


 Highly Desirable

 

 




 




Foundational institutional knowledge of State of Michigan platforms, cloud architecture, security requirements and processes.


 1-3 years

 

 




Cloud security and compliance experience


 
Highly Desirable

 

 




Certification(s):
Google – Cloud Certified Cloud Digital Leader
               AWS – Certified Cloud Practitioner
 


 Highly Desirable

 

 




 


 

 

 




 
Core Competencies


Ability to learn and apply cloud engineering concepts quickly.


Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills.


Ability to interpret technical requirements and assist in developing cloud-based solutions.


Interest in automation, DevOps, and continuous improvement.


Clear communication skills for explaining technical concepts to both technical and non‑technical audiences.


Collaborative mindset and willingness to work across teams.


Other desired skills: Containerization, Linux, Database skills, security and recovery, web services and applications programming interfaces (APIs)


 
Core Tasks


Assist senior cloud architects with the design and deployment of cloud solutions across the State of Michigan AWS, and GCP environments.


Support the build‑out of multi‑cloud environments, including public, private, and hybrid cloud models.


Help maintain and troubleshoot cloud infrastructure components.


Contribute to the development and maintenance of CI/CD pipelines.


Assist with infrastructure provisioning and configuration using automation tools.


Participate in integrating cloud pipelines with existing DevOps systems.


Document architecture decisions, pipeline configurations, and deployment procedures.


Participate in knowledge transfer sessions and training activities.


Maintain clear and organized technical documentation for onboarding and future reference.


Support adherence to cloud security best practices and compliance frameworks (NIST, CIS, PCI, etc.).


Assist in implementing secure configurations and monitoring controls.


Work with cross‑functional teams to understand business needs and translate them into cloud requirements.


Participate in discussions with vendors, product specialists, and internal teams to evaluate technologies.


Support enterprise architecture reviews and solution assessments.


 Assist with performance analysis, troubleshooting, and optimization of cloud workloads.


Help design and test workload migrations and disaster recovery scenarios.


Support integration of cloud services with on-premises technologies (VMware, Cisco, Dell, Nutanix, etc.).


Leverage State of Michigan Institutional knowledge to cloud engineering projects.

This role is ideal for a developer who can build reliable applications, create meaningful dashboards, work with SQL-based data, and translate business needs into practical technical solutions. Gather requirements from stakeholders and convert business needs into clear, reliable technical solutions.

Modernize legacy reports, workflows, and applications where appropriate.

jobs.description: This position is part of the Indiana Department of Health Laboratory, Antimicrobial Resistance Lab Network.Purpose of Position/Summary:Incumbent is responsible for coordinating and performing the full range of microbiological examinations and analyses including culture, biochemical tests, PCR, and WGS of clinical specimens for isolation and identification of bacteria and yeast  including but not limited to E.coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumanii, and Candida auris. Incumbent will also be responsible for the documentation of all quality control and quality assurance activities according to CLIA regulations. In addition, this position may cross-train in other areas of the lab that may include molecular, microbiological, viral, serological, and other techniques to support routine testing and provide backup capacity.Essential Duties/Responsibilities:Incumbent will have in-depth knowledge and ability in the area of microbiology and molecular biology and is able to perform laboratory associated assays or the ability to learn these techniques upon successful completion of proficiency testing.  Representative duties include:• Conducting examinations of samples and/or reference samples for analyses such as but not limited to, molecular detection or isolation and identification of microorganisms or their nucleic acids.• Strictly follow the laboratory's procedures for specimen handling and processing, test analyses, reporting and maintaining records of patient test results.• Extraction of nucleic acids from specimens, isolates, and samples via a variety of manual and automated methods;•Utilize molecular techniques such as, but not limited to, PCR, sequencing, MALDI-TOF, and WGS;• Evaluate, interpret, and validate laboratory results and reports findings.• Maintain laboratory record system of submitted samples and specimens and their possible referral.• Conduct quality control checks on laboratory methods, materials, and equipment in strict adherence to the laboratory's quality control policies. • Maintain an inventory of laboratory supplies and order as needed to ensure testing needs are met. • Assist in preparations of epidemiological and/or statistical reports from data compiled on a daily, weekly, monthly, or annual basis.• Maintain competency in all trained areas.• Perform all related work as required.•Testing personnel responsibilities (493.1495 Standard):    The testing personnel are responsible for specimen processing, test performance and for reporting test results.    (a)    Each individual performs only those high complexity tests that are authorized by the laboratory director and require a degree of skill       commensurate with the individual’s education, training or experience, and technical abilities.    (b)    Each individual performing high complexity testing must—        (1)    Follow the laboratory’s procedures for specimen handling and            processing, test analyses, reporting and maintaining records of patient             test results;         (2)    Maintain records that demonstrate that proficiency testing samples are             tested in the same manner as patient specimens;        (3)    Adhere to the laboratory’s quality control policies, document all quality             control activities, instrument and procedural calibrations and             maintenance performed;        (4)    Follow the laboratory’s established policies and procedures whenever            test systems are not within the laboratory’s established acceptable levels            of performance;        (5)    Be capable of identifying problems that may adversely affect test            performance or reporting of test results and either must correct the            problems or immediately notify the general supervisor, technical            supervisor, clinical consultant, or director;        (6)    Document all corrective actions taken when test systems deviate from            the laboratory’s established performance specifications; and        (7)    Except as specified in paragraph (c) of this section, if qualified under §            493.1489(b)(5), perform high complexity testing only under the onsite,            direct supervision of a general supervisor qualified under § 493.1461.    (c)    Exception. For individuals qualified under § 493.1489(b)(5), who were performing        high complexity testing on or before January 19, 1993, the requirements of        paragraph (b)(7) of this section are not effective, provided that all high complexity        testing performed by the individual in the absence of a general supervisor is        reviewed within   hours by a general supervisor qualified under § 493.1461.Job Requirements:• Extensive knowledge of the principles, theories and practices of microbiology and related sub- specialties;• Specialized knowledge of current scientific methods and testing procedures and the ability to apply them when seeking solutions to public health laboratory problems;• Specialized knowledge of and ability to use a full range of standard technical equipment, complex scientific apparatus, and automated techniques of analysis;• Extensive knowledge of laboratory safety practices and principles;• Aware of state and federal laws, rules, regulations, and policies concerning the program area (i.e. CLIA); • Ability to meet requirements for personnel certification as a technologist pursuant to the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act (CLIA)• Ability to effectively communicate technical information both verbally and in writing and maintain productive working relationships;• Ability to satisfactorily participate in proficiency testing programs and recognize QA problems;• Ability to compile, analyze, evaluate, and prepare laboratory reports.Supervisory Responsibilities/Direct Reports:N/ADifficulty of Work:Incumbent is engaged in scientific analyses that demand accuracy and demonstrated proficiency in applying laboratory analytical skills to select pertinent guidelines and formulated plans for problem solving.  Projects involve many complex variables of great intricacy and the microbiologist is often called upon to analyze and identify unusual specimens/samples. Work requires use of analytical judgment and technical knowledge in order to draw accurate, logical conclusions. Incumbent will also be required to develop and research new testing procedures.Responsibility:Incumbent works independently as an expert in the assigned area. Technical and/or detailed instruction is provided only upon request when necessitated by a procedural change and/or special project.  Incumbent maintains established safety practices when working with materials that have a chemical hazard or biohazard potential.  Reports are reviewed for general technical accuracy; however, tasks are performed independently.  Errors in work could adversely affect the health, safety and well being of the incumbent or coworkers.Personal Work Relationships:Incumbent works with supervisor and with other State Department of Health staff such as Laboratory Safety Officer and/or external entities (e.g. local health departments, etc.) to devise and implement work procedures and information dissemination.  Individual will have contact with employees and the public as a laboratory expert and in the explanation of laboratory procedures and recommendations when appropriate.Physical Effort:The required personal protective equipment can be cumbersome and awkward. Extra effort and concentration will be necessary to perform routine laboratory manipulations under these conditions.  Working Conditions:The incumbent will be performing tests on potentially dangerous specimens. jobs.title: Business Analyst 5
jobs.description:
DTMB Agency Services needs a Business Analyst 5 to provide excellent customer service supporting both project and work request needs for the Environment, Great Lakes and Energy (EGLE) Agency. 
Key responsibilities include being the liaison between DTMB and the project stakeholders, as well as providing expert facilitation and elicitation and process modeling to help develop strategy and requirements for ongoing enhancements and related work projects.  In addition, as part of the overall support for EGLE, this person will be a critical member of the DTMB Agency Services Business Analyst team, participating in various related work requests for EGLE and contributing to the operational activities of the BA team.
Customer service and being a champion to ease Agency compliance with DTMB policies and practices are key performance expectations for this person.  They must be able to quickly gain a working understanding of applicable constraints and enablers and help EGLE navigate those for the success for their projects and work requests. 
DTMB Agency Services and EGLE welcomes candidates that are self-directed, well organized, confident in their ability to build relationships, quick to come up to speed on new assignments, and able to be flexible and adaptable to changing needs and/or direction.

jobs.title: Network Engineer 3
jobs.description:
Network Engineer supporting hybrid infrastructure. Manages routing, switching, firewalls,VPN,SD-WAN,andnetwork security;supports monitoring, troubleshooting, resiliency, and secure connectivity. 
Local Candidates strongly preferred 

Position Overview

The Virginia Office of the Attorney General (OAG) seeks a Network Engineer to support and maintain a secure, stable, and high-performing enterprise network environment. This role is responsible for administering and troubleshooting core networking infrastructure across multiple office locations, data centers, and remote access environments.

The Network Engineer is a hands-on technical role responsible for routing, switching, firewalls, VPN connectivity, wireless infrastructure, and network resiliency. The position works under the direction of the Director of Infrastructure & Operations and collaborates with Infrastructure, Information Security, End User Services, Application/Data Services, vendors, and service providers.

This role emphasizes operational discipline, secure network design, structured change management, and reliable service delivery within a government environment.

Key Responsibilities

Network Infrastructure Administration
 

Administer enterprise routing and switching infrastructure
Configure and maintain LAN, WAN, wireless, and remote access environments
Support hybrid MPLS and SD-WAN connectivity across multiple locations
Maintain network availability, resiliency, and performance

Firewall & Secure Connectivity Management


Administer firewalls, VPN solutions, and secure remote connectivity
Implement and maintain network segmentation and access controls
Support secure connectivity for cloud and hybrid environments
Coordinate firewall rule changes and network security updates

Monitoring & Troubleshooting


Monitor network health, utilization, and performance
Respond to outages, connectivity issues, and infrastructure incidents
Perform network troubleshooting across routing, switching, wireless, and VPN environments
Conduct root cause analysis and implement corrective actions


Security & Compliance Support

Support implementation of network security controls and standards
Collaborate with the Information Security Office on vulnerability remediation and risk reduction
Assist with logging, monitoring, and audit activities
Support secure configuration and hardening practices

Change Management & Operations


Execute network changes through defined change management processes
Validate planned changes and maintain rollback procedures
Participate in maintenance windows and operational planning
Maintain network documentation and diagrams

Vendor & Carrier Coordination


Coordinate with telecommunications providers and vendors
Support circuit provisioning, troubleshooting, and escalations
Assist with hardware lifecycle and support renewals


Cross-Team Collaboration
 

Partner with Systems Administration on infrastructure dependencies
Coordinate with End User Services regarding user-impacting network issues
Support Application/Data teams with connectivity and performance needs
Communicate operational risks and system impacts to leadership

Required Qualifications


Experience administering enterprise network environments
Strong knowledge of routing and switching concepts
Experience with firewalls, VPNs, and secure remote access
Experience troubleshooting network connectivity and performance issues
Familiarity with wireless networking technologies
Understanding of structured operational and change management processes

Preferred Qualifications
 

Experience with Cisco networking technologies
Experience with SD-WAN and hybrid network environments
Experience in government or regulated environments
Familiarity with network monitoring and logging tools
Knowledge of security frameworks such as NIST
Relevant certifications such as CCNA or CCNP

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities


oting and analytical skills
Ability to manage multiple operational priorities
Effective written and verbal communication skills
Ability to work collaboratively across technical teams
Focus on reliability, security, and operational consistency

Working Conditions
 

Office-based environment
Occasional after-hours support for maintenance or incident response
Limited travel between office locations may be required


Additional Information

This position supports the agency’s core network infrastructure and plays a critical role in ensuring secure and reliable connectivity for agency operations. The Network Engineer operates within established governance and operational processes to support stability, resiliency, and risk reduction across the enterprise environment.

jobs.title: IN-IDOI-Inbound Call Center Rep
jobs.description:
Must complete a 5-day training on health insurance for people with Medicare. Answers 800 helpline calls and performs other general office duties such as data entry, mailings, and inventory.


OVERVIEW
Answer in-coming 800 helpline calls, transfer calls to volunteers when available, data entry of client contacts, and other clerical functions such as mailings and inventory.

DUTIES
*Answer all 800 calls in a timely manner. Record on Client Contact forms.
*Forward 800 calls to available volunteer counselors or provide counseling assistance when volunteers are not available. Take calls from counselors regarding availability and/or supplies.
*Complete data entry each day including Client Contacts
*Do labels and mailing for information packets, assemble packets of information, and make copies of SHIP information as needed.
*Inform the Office Manager when supplies of materials are low
*Put away all deliveries in an orderly manner. Keep work area in order and recycle unwanted paper and boxes. Make sure work area is neat and orderly
*Take voice mail messages for all packet requests twice a day (morning and afternoon at minimum).
*Forward call back messages to Volunteer Supervisors at the end of the day.
*Put together new counselor training materials and other training materials requested by Trainers.
*Put together presentation materials and supplies as requested by Volunteer Supervisors, Counselors, or SHIP Local Sites.
*Other duties as assigned by Office Manager including, but not limited to, special mailings/emails, 800 message recordings, updating lists, etc.

DIFFICULTY OF WORK
Incumbent performs standardized tasks and must successfully complete trainings and effectively communicate on the telephone keeping consistent with agency policies and laws affecting the agency.

RESPONSIBILITY
Incumbent must provide accurate and correct information to callers and complete tasks in a timely manner. Incumbent is responsible for accuracy giving Medicare information over the telephone and maintaining accurate records, files, forms, reports and technical information. Errors in work or faulty judgment can undermine trust and the reputation of the program.

PERSONAL WORK RELATIONSHIPS
Personal work relationships are with immediate office staff, Office Supervisor, the public, department and agency representatives at local and state levels. Contacts are for the purpose of relaying and giving information and making referrals.
